title: Random/Multiple Cylinder Misfire Detected
detail: One or more engine cylinders are misfiring, causing the engine to run unevenly. Common causes include faulty spark plugs, ignition coils, fuel injectors, camshaft/crankshaft position sensors, or air-fuel mixture issues.
implications: If left unresolved, this can reduce engine performance and fuel economy and increase harmful emissions. In severe cases it may damage the catalytic converter.
suggestedActions: Check and replace spark plugs and wires if necessary
Test ignition coils and replace if necessary
Test camshaft and crankshaft position sensors

title: Catalyst System Efficiency Below Threshold
detail: The efficiency of the catalytic converter is below the manufacturer-defined threshold. May be caused by a failing catalytic converter, faulty oxygen sensor, exhaust leaks, or fuel injection issues.
implications: Increased tailpipe emissions, failed emission tests, decreased fuel economy, and potential long-term engine damage.
suggestedActions: Check and replace the catalytic converter if necessary
Inspect the exhaust system for leaks

title: System Too Lean (Bank 1)
detail: The air-fuel mixture has too much air and not enough fuel. Possible causes: vacuum leak, faulty MAF sensor, fuel pressure problems, or a defective oxygen sensor.
implications: Poor vehicle performance, higher emissions, and potential engine damage if left unresolved.
suggestedActions: Clean or replace the MAF sensor

title: Oxygen Sensor Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1, Sensor 2)
detail: Malfunction in the circuit of the downstream oxygen sensor. Usually a faulty sensor, damaged wiring, or loose connectors.
implications: Reduced fuel efficiency, sub-optimal engine performance, and increased emissions.
suggestedActions: Check and replace the oxygen sensor
Inspect wiring and connectors to the sensor

title: Camshaft Position Sensor Circuit Malfunction
detail: Issue in the 'A' circuit of the camshaft position sensor. Causes include a faulty sensor, wiring issues, or a worn timing belt/chain.
implications: Engine stalling, hard starting, or engine damage in severe cases.
suggestedActions: Replace the camshaft position sensor if necessary

title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Circuit Malfunction
detail: Fault in the Intake Manifold Runner Control (IMRC) circuit, often a faulty IMRC solenoid/actuator or wiring harness issue.
implications: Power loss, stalling, or increased emissions. Repair promptly to prevent further damage.
suggestedActions: Inspect and replace the IMRC solenoid
Inspect the wiring harness and connectors

title: Coolant Thermostat Malfunction
detail: The coolant thermostat may be stuck open, or the engine coolant temperature sensor is faulty.
implications: Increased fuel consumption, poor engine performance, and potential damage from overcooling or overheating.

title: Brake Switch A/B Correlation
detail: Discrepancy between the 'A' and 'B' brake switch signals. Causes: faulty brake switch, blown fuse, or wiring issues.
implications: Can affect cruise control and ABS, impacting driving safety.

title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor Low Input
detail: Input from the A/C refrigerant pressure sensor is abnormally low, usually due to low refrigerant from leaks or a faulty sensor.
implications: Air conditioning works inefficiently; prolonged neglect can damage the A/C system.

title: EVAP System Small Leak Detected
detail: A small leak in the evaporative emission control system. Most commonly a loose or faulty fuel cap, or a cracked EVAP hose.
implications: Increased fuel vapor emissions and a possible failed emissions test. Not an immediate drivability concern.
suggestedActions: Tighten or replace the fuel cap

title: EVAP System Large Leak Detected
detail: A large leak in the evaporative emission control system, often a missing fuel cap or a stuck-open purge/vent valve.
implications: Fuel smell, increased emissions, failed emissions test.
suggestedActions: Test the purge and vent valves

title: EGR Flow Insufficient
detail: The exhaust gas recirculation system is not flowing enough exhaust gas, usually due to a clogged EGR valve or passages.
implications: Higher NOx emissions, possible engine knock, and reduced performance.
suggestedActions: Clean or replace the EGR valve

title: Mass Air Flow Sensor Range/Performance
detail: The MAF sensor reading is outside the expected range, often caused by a dirty sensor or an intake air leak.
implications: Poor fuel economy, rough idle, and reduced power.

title: Vehicle Speed Sensor Malfunction
detail: The ECU is receiving no or implausible signal from the vehicle speed sensor.
implications: Speedometer may stop working and transmission shifting or ABS can be affected.

title: Knock Sensor Circuit Malfunction
detail: Fault in the knock sensor circuit, which detects engine knock/pre-ignition.
implications: The ECU cannot protect the engine from knock, risking engine damage under load and reduced performance.
suggestedActions: Inspect knock sensor wiring and connector

title: Transmission Control System Malfunction
detail: Generic code indicating the transmission control module has detected a fault and requested the check engine light.
implications: Transmission may enter limp mode with harsh shifting or limited gears.
suggestedActions: Read transmission-specific codes with a capable scanner
Check transmission fluid level and condition

title: Lost Communication with ECM/PCM
detail: A control module has lost communication with the engine control module over the CAN bus.
implications: Can cause no-start conditions or loss of critical vehicle functions. Needs prompt diagnosis.
suggestedActions: Check CAN bus wiring and connectors
Scan all modules for related codes
